descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1897
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897, renominating its 1896 candidate

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1897
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1893 to 1897

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Prohibition, a Socialist, a Socialist Labor and a dissident People's party nominee (answer "other").
never_name: McKinley, Bryan, Roosevelt, Stevenson, Woolley, Debs, Hanna or Cleveland

slice_sources.men: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1900 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); women 21+ outside the South; women could vote for president only in Wyoming, Colorado (1893), Utah and Idaho (1896).
slice_sources.south-white: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1900 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement was intensifying (Mississippi 1890, South Carolina 1895, Louisiana's 1898 grandfather clause, North Carolina's August 1900 amendment); the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1900 census (Twelfth Census); foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
